newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Shell Nigeria says it recognises Ogoni rights group.
newsitem.headline: Shell Nigeria says it recognises Ogoni rights group.

text.p: Royal Dutch Shell's Nigeria unit on Friday dissociated itself from a local newspaper report which said it did not recognise executed author Ken Saro-Wiwa's Movement for the Survival of Ogoni Peoples (MOSOP).
Saro-Wiwa and eight other MOSOP activists were hanged last year for murder by Nigeria in defiance of international opinion.
"The Shell Petroleum Development Company of Nigeria strongly denies today's front page story in Thisday newspaper that states the company does not recognise MOSOP," it said in a statement.

"Shell has consistently stressed that it is willing to talk to all parties and factions involved in the Ogoni issue. So far, we have talked to a wide range of Ogoni people and organisations including chiefs, local government area chairmen, the Concerned Ogoni Leaders of Thought, and leaders of MOSOP at various times."

The paper had quoted a Shell spokesman as telling reporters in the oil city of Port-Harcourt that Shell did not recognise MOSOP, which has long demanded self-determination for the 500,000 Ogonis and compensation from Shell for damage it says Shell's operations caused the local environment.
Shell quit Ogoniland in 1993, after alleging sabotage of its installations and attacks on its staff by MOSOP militants.
The statement said Shell had begun talks with the Ogonis "to help in the process of reconciliation... (and) tackle problems facing the Ogoni people."
"We have offered to return to help clean up oil spills that have happened since the company withdrew in 1993, rehabilitate past community projects and discuss new projects with communities."
